claims.text: The untreated HEA exhibits high friction across a wide temperature range.
The untreated HEA exhibits high wear across a wide temperature range.
A single-step controlled thermal oxidation treatment under calibrated oxygen partial pressure will form a spinel oxide layer on the HEA surface.
The resulting spinel oxide layer will be ultrathin and adherent.
The oxide film can be formed reproducibly by tailoring the oxidation atmosphere.
The spinel oxide film will remain stable from ambient temperature to approximately 500°C.
A surface oxide layer can act as a protective barrier that improves HEA wear resistance at elevated temperature.
The spinel oxide layer is lubricious and minimizes direct asperity contact between moving surfaces.
The spinel oxide layer lowers interfacial shear stress and distributes contact load.
The treated alloy will have a coefficient of friction approximately 20–30% below that of the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will have a wear rate approximately 50% below that of the untreated alloy.
The predicted friction and wear reductions will persist across the full range from ambient temperature to approximately 500°C.
Untreated HEAs form absent or non-optimized oxide layers that lead to higher friction and wear under variable temperatures.
Substantial deviations in oxygen partial pressure or heating rate may prevent formation of the optimal spinel film and eliminate the benefit.
The treatment may cease to be effective outside the ambient-to-500°C operating range.
Precise process parameters needed to obtain the ideal film thickness and adherence are not fully established.
